measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorize up to $624 million in bonds for listed Grossmont and Cuyamaca college facilities, including career-training classrooms, asbestos and mold removal, wildfire and campus safety, building repairs, technology and other capital projects. Property taxes would repay principal and interest. The district estimates $45 million annually, an average rate of $24.67 and highest rate of $24.98 per $100,000 of assessed value, collection through fiscal 2058–59, and approximately $1,246,250,216 total repayment. It does not expect the new bonds to increase the overall $37.52 rate levied in fiscal 2025–26, but the estimates are not legal tax caps or binding repayment promises. Interest rates must stay within legal limits. Money must stay local and cannot pay teacher or administrator salaries or other operating expenses. Independent citizen oversight, annual financial and performance audits and public reports are required. State matching funds and completion of every listed project are not guaranteed. Approval requires 55% of votes.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Authorize the district to borrow up to $624 million for the listed college facilities and levy property taxes to repay the bonds under these conditions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize these bonds through this measure.
